newsitem.title: USA: Drug company defends weight loss drug warnings.
newsitem.headline: Drug company defends weight loss drug warnings.

text.p: Wyeth-Ayerst Laboratories on Thursday denied allegations it failed to warn users about possible side effects of its popular prescription weight loss drugs.

Two law firms filed a class action lawsuit in federal court in San Francisco on Wednesday against nine companies that make or market three diet drugs alleging they failed to give adequate warnings to their customers.

One of the companies named was Wyeth-Ayerst, a division of American Home Products Corp, which markets dexfenfluramine, a diet drug sold under the brand name Redux, and fenfluramine, known by the name Pondimin.
In a statement, the company said it had not yet been served with the lawsuit, but said it "rejects the allegations ... that it failed to provide appropriate warnings on the use of these products."
"The Food and Drug Administration has approved the sale of each of these drugs and has at all times approved the warnings provided by Wyeth-Ayerst," the company said.
The company said it planned to "vigorously" contest the allegations.

The class action lawsuit was filed a day after researchers at the Mayo Clinic announced that two of the diet drugs -- fenfluramine and phentermine -- may have been responsible for a thickening of the heart valves in at least 24 young women.

The suit, filed on behalf of two users of the diet drugs, seeks unspecified compensatory and punitive damages. It also seeks medical monitoring to enable people who have taken the drugs to "monitor the existence of dangerous potential side effects caused by the drugs, including primary pulmonary hypertension and valvular heart disease."

Wyeth-Ayerst said the two drugs it markets "can play an important role in treating clinically obese patients when prescribed as part of a physician-directed program that also includes a regulated diet and increased exercise."
